newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-CUFFY MAKES IMMEDIATE IMPACT IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CUFFY MAKES IMMEDIATE IMPACT IN FINAL.

text.p: West Indies fast bowler Cameron Cuffy made an immediate impact in his first tour match as Pakistan laboured to 165 all out in 48.3 overs in the second World Series limited overs final on Monday.
Cuffy, who arrived in Australia on Saturday as a replacement for injured pacemen Nixon McLean and Kenneth Benjamin, claimed two wickets after being rushed into the side.

Pakistan, needing a victory to clinch the triangular competition, struggled from the outset after captain Wasim Akram won the toss and elected to bat on a lively pitch in sweltering heat at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Cuffy ensured Pakistan opener Aamir Sohail experienced a miserable return to the side from a one-match suspension for dissent by dismissing the hard-hitting left-hander for 16.
Ijaz Ahmed, the top scorer in Pakistan's four-wicket win in Sydney in the first of the best-of-three final on Saturday, scored 45 to bolster the middle order.
Ijaz's innings made amends for his role in the bizarre run-out of fellow batsman Inzamam-ul-Haq for five.
When both players found themselves at the same end after a breakdown in communication, West Indies vice-captain Brian Lara removed the bails at the bowler's end.
But neither Inzamam nor Ijaz accepted responsibility for the dismissal. Both batsmen refused to budge from the middle, each blaming the other.

After standing side by side in the crease for three minutes and watching several replays of the incident on a giant screen at the ground, it was Inzamam who was eventually ordered back to the pavilion by the umpires for failing to recover his ground.

West Indies all-rounder Phil Simmons, another player recently summoned from the Caribbean in response to the tourists' injury crisis, eventually removed Ijaz by tempting him to edge a faint catch to wicketkeeper Junior Murray.

Mohammad Wasim lifted the scoring rate by hitting 41 before becoming the last wicket to fall in an innings that failed to gather any momentum after West Indies captain Courtney Walsh dismissed opener Shahid Afridi and number three Zahoor Elahi for ducks.
